australia.fact: Aboriginal Australians have lived in Australia for at least 50,000 years and have one of the oldest continuing cultures on Earth.
australia.ask: Which country's Aboriginal peoples have one of the oldest continuing cultures, over 50,000 years?

australia.fact: The Sydney Opera House in Australia, with roofs shaped like sails, opened in 1973.
australia.ask: Which country's famous Opera House, with roofs shaped like sails, opened in 1973?

australia.fact: In 1770 Captain James Cook sailed along the east coast of Australia and landed at Botany Bay.
australia.ask: Which country's east coast did Captain James Cook sail along in 1770, landing at Botany Bay?

new-zealand.fact: Edmund Hillary of New Zealand and Tenzing Norgay were the first people known to reach the top of Mount Everest, in 1953.
new-zealand.ask: Which country was Edmund Hillary from, one of the first two people to climb Mount Everest?

new-zealand.fact: Māori voyagers from eastern Polynesia sailed canoes to New Zealand and settled there in the 1200s and 1300s, among the last big lands people reached.
new-zealand.ask: Which country was settled by Māori voyagers from Polynesia in the 1200s and 1300s?

papua-new-guinea.fact: At Kuk Swamp in Papua New Guinea, people were farming crops like bananas and taro about 7,000 years ago or more, one of the earliest farming sites in the world.
papua-new-guinea.ask: Which country's Kuk Swamp shows that people there were farming about 7,000 years ago or more?

fiji.fact: Levuka, Fiji's first colonial capital, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with old buildings from the 1800s.
fiji.ask: Which country's town of Levuka, its first colonial capital, is a World Heritage Site?

tonga.fact: Tonga is the only island kingdom in the Pacific that was never fully colonized by a foreign power.
tonga.ask: Which island kingdom in the Pacific was never fully colonized by a foreign power?

kiribati.fact: In 1995 Kiribati moved the International Date Line so all of its islands, spread over a huge stretch of ocean, would share the same calendar day.
kiribati.ask: Which country moved the International Date Line in 1995 so all its islands share the same day?

south-pole.fact: The Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station, first built by the United States in 1956, is named after Roald Amundsen and Robert Falcon Scott, the first two explorers to reach the South Pole.
south-pole.ask: Where did the US build a research station in 1956, named after explorers Amundsen and Scott?

mount-vinson.fact: Mount Vinson was first climbed in December 1966 by an American team led by Nicholas Clinch. It is named after US congressman Carl Vinson.
mount-vinson.ask: Which Antarctic mountain was first climbed in 1966 and is named after a US congressman?

mount-erebus.fact: Mount Erebus was first climbed in 1908 by members of Ernest Shackleton's expedition. It is named after HMS Erebus, one of James Clark Ross's ships.
mount-erebus.ask: Which Antarctic volcano was first climbed by members of Shackleton's team in 1908?

ross-ice-shelf.fact: In 1929 Richard Byrd took off from his base, Little America, on the Ross Ice Shelf and made the first flight over the South Pole.
ross-ice-shelf.ask: From a base on which ice shelf did Richard Byrd take off in 1929 to fly over the South Pole?

antarctic-peninsula.fact: In January 1820 Edward Bransfield sighted the tip of the Antarctic Peninsula, one of the first sightings of the Antarctic mainland.
antarctic-peninsula.ask: Which part of Antarctica did Edward Bransfield spot in 1820, among the first sightings of the continent?

deception-island.fact: In 1928 Hubert Wilkins made the first airplane flight in Antarctica, taking off from Deception Island.
deception-island.ask: From which Antarctic island did Hubert Wilkins make the first airplane flight in Antarctica, in 1928?

lake-vostok.fact: Vostok Station, on the ice above Lake Vostok, recorded the coldest natural temperature ever measured on Earth: minus 89.2 degrees Celsius, in July 1983.
lake-vostok.ask: Above which hidden lake is the station that recorded Earth's coldest measured temperature, in 1983?

weddell-sea.fact: The Weddell Sea is named after James Weddell, a British sealer who sailed into it in 1823 and reached farther south than anyone before.
weddell-sea.ask: Which Antarctic sea did a British sealer sail into in 1823, getting farther south than anyone before?

lambert-glacier.fact: After Australian expeditions mapped the area in 1956, the Lambert Glacier was named after Bruce Lambert, Australia's director of national mapping.
lambert-glacier.ask: Which Antarctic glacier was named after an Australian mapmaker following Australian mapping in 1956?
